# Multiple correlation test

Calculates correlations between multiple variables.

## Usage

``` r
mcor_test(
  x,
  y = NULL,
  estimate = TRUE,
  p.value = FALSE,
  method = "spearman",
  method_adjust = "BH"
)
```

## Arguments

- x:

  Data frame of numerical variables.

- y:

  Data frame of numerical variables. If `NULL`, correlations are
  calculated within `x`.

- estimate:

  Logical indicating whether to return correlation coefficients.

- p.value:

  Logical indicating whether to return adjusted p-values.

- method:

  Character specifying the correlation method: `pearson`, `kendall`, or
  `spearman`.

- method_adjust:

  Character specifying the p-value adjustment method.

## Value

List containing two data frames corresponding to correlation
coefficients and p-values.

## Examples

``` r
library(magrittr)
x0 <- runif(20)
x <- lapply(
    c(1, -1),
    function(i) sapply(seq(10), function(j) x0 * i + runif(10, max = 1))
) %>%
    Reduce(cbind, .) %>%
    set_colnames(paste("Variable", seq(20)))
y <- lapply(
    c(1, -1),
    function(i) sapply(seq(10), function(j) x0 * i + runif(10, max = 1))
) %>%
    Reduce(cbind, .) %>%
    set_colnames(paste("Variable", seq(20))) %>%
    .[, seq(5)]
mcor_test(x)
```
